title: Croquetas de Jamón
description: A stiff béchamel worked through with finely chopped ham, chilled until it slices, then breaded and fried into short cylinders. Makes about twenty.
notes: The paste must be cold and firm before you shape anything. No amount of extra flour will make a warm béchamel hold a cylinder.

ingredients.name: serrano ham
ingredients.note: chopped as fine as you have patience for

steps.text: Sweat the onion in the butter over a low heat until it is soft and has taken no colour at all.
Stir in the plain flour and cook the raw taste out of it, then add the warm milk a splash at a time, beating it smooth before the next one goes in.
steps.tip: Add the milk faster than this and you will spend the rest of the evening chasing lumps around the pan.

steps.text: Beat until the paste comes away from the sides in one mass, then fold through the serrano ham and season with the nutmeg, salt, and white pepper.
Spread it thin in a tray, press cling film onto the surface, and chill it until it is firm enough to cut.
Cut the cold paste into strips and roll each strip into a short cylinder between floured palms.
Pass each croqueta through the plain flour, then the beaten eggs, then the breadcrumbs, pressing the crumbs on firmly.
Chill the breaded croquetas again while the neutral oil comes up to temperature.
steps.tip: The second chill is what stops them splitting. A croqueta that bursts in the pan was warm going in.

steps.text: Fry them a few at a time until they are deep gold, then drain them standing on end so the bottoms stay crisp.
